LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains standard AUR package source definitions using git+URL references to the official GitHub repository (https://github.com/rafaeldominiquini/mimixbox). The `source`, `source_x86_64`, and `source_aarch64` variables point to pre-built tarballs hosted on the same repository's releases page. During `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`, the build system will fetch these tarballs from the official upstream source and verify checksums — both of which are normal and expected steps in the AUR build process.

The top-level `verify()` function performs checksum validation after extraction, which is a standard security practice. There are no malicious elements such as:
- Network requests to untrusted/unrelated hosts
- Obfuscated or encoded commands
- Execution of external scripts or shell commands
- Attempts to exfiltrate data or run unauthorized code
- Unpinned VCS references or skipped checksums (all three checksums are explicitly provided)

Since the `--nobuild` and `--noprepare` flags prevent `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` from executing, no code outside the PKGBUILD itself can run during these stages. The only code that executes is the built-in `verify()` function, which is purely for integrity checking and is safe.

Therefore, running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` is safe.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>The PKGBUILD uses standard VCS source definitions pointing to the official GitHub repository with explicit checksums. The `--nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` flags ensure no build/execution occurs, and the only code that runs is the standard `verify()` function for checksum validation — which is safe.</summary>
